That on 16.11.2023 at about 04.30 PM., the petitioner was driving the two wheeler bearing Reg No.KA- 53-HQ-6616 in Kolar - Bangalore NH-75, near Kolthur Gate,
Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, wherein the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg No.MH-10-DT- 4485 drove it, in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner from the back side and caused accident.

In the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries, he was shifted to Kempanna Hospital,
wherein he took first aid treatment, later he was shifted to MTB hospital, wherein he took treatment for the accidental injuries as an inpatient and he has spent Rs.5,00,000/- for his medical treatment.
3. Petitioner stated that he is 50 years of age working as a Quality checking supervisor in a company and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month,

Further he stated that the accident has occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.297/2023 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

He alleged that the Respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle, he insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such both are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent no.1 appeared through his counsel filed the power and written statement by denying the entire petition averments in toto.
He contended that the insured has violated the policy conditions as such they are not liable to pay the compensation.
Respondent No.2 has not chosen to contest the petition and he is placed exparte.
5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined another two witness as PW.2 and PW3 and produced and marked 28 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 28 and they are fully cross examined.

6. Respondent no.1 has chosen to lead the evidence, there is no material on record to show that the respondent No.1 is prevented from appearing before this tribunal to lead his evidence hence respondent no.1 evidence is taken as nil.
7. I have heard the arguments from both the counsels appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

8. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that on 16.11.2023 at about 04.30 PM, he was driving a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-HQ-6616, on Kolar - Bangalore NH-75 Road,
near Kolathuru Gate, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural district, wherein the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg No.MH-10-DT-4485 drove it, with speed, rash and Muniraju N vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100821828/
2 negligent manner, and dashed against the petitioner vehicle from back side and caused the accident and thereby Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the said accident?
2.Whether respondent No.1 proves that the, driver of the offending vehicle has not holding valid driving license as on the date of accident as contended at para No.6 of the written statement ?

The aforesaid facts establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The final report which is at Ex.P7 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary which are at Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.10.
The said documents reveals that the petitioner has sustained crash injury and bone fracture on his left leg.
Further it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for 9 days for the accidental injuries in the MTB hospital, Bangalore.
Further it reveals that left leg amputation, that is below the knee and stump closure was done on 16.11.2023 under anesthesia and they knee stump measuring 14 inches.
Ex.P11 is the medical bills which shows that petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.3,33,468/-.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

14. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
15. Petitioner took treatment at MTB hospital as an inpatient for 9 days and left leg was amputed.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 & 3 to disbelieve the fact that he has sustained the injuries in the alleged accident and he took treatment for the same.
Inasmuch the wound certificate, discharge summary and the medical reports and bills issued form the hospital has to be accepted.
The oral testimony PW-3 corroborates with discharge summary and wound certificate and his report and X-ray which is at Ex.P.27 and 28.

Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment and under went surgery and he was in patent for nine days for attendant charges, transportation,
nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- in addition to actual medical expenses of Rs.3,33,468/-.
Petitioner is entitled for Rs. 3,53,468/-under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
16. According to the petitioner, he was working as a Quality checking supervisor at Y cook company and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

PW-2 is the employer he has tendered the employment letter, pay slips of petitioner as per Ex.P.22 and 26, as per the said documents the last gross salary of the petitioner in the month of November 2023 was Rs.20,533/-.
He has tendered the releaving letter of the petitioner as per Ex.P24, it reveals that petitioner was releaved from the Job on 16.01.2023.b
Accordingly the monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.20,333/-, that is after deducting the professional tax.
As per the income tax slab for the assessment year 2024-25, the petitioner income will not comes under taxable limits.
Considering the nature of the injury and amputation done to the petitioner.
I am of view that at-least 3 months he has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.20,333/- X 3 months = Rs.60,999/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability and future prospectus.
17. The petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him.
He examined an orthopedic surgeon Dr.B.N.Nagaraj as PW-3.

He deposed that, petitioner's left leg has been amputated and stump length is 14 inches as per Ex.P.27 and he assessed the physical disability of the petitioner as 85% to the whole body and it is permanent disability.

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the respondents argued that the assessment of PW-3 is on higher side.
I have perused the evidence of PW-3 wound certificate, discharge summary, X-ray etc.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctor who has treated him in the hospital.

It is true that petitioner sustained the grievous injuries and his left leg is amputated by way of surgery, further doctor has deposed that petitioner could not walk independently and he could not perform his supervisory work.
It is true that petitioner could not perform his supervisory work or any other work independently with a limping leg.
Further it is also true that petitioner has lost his earning capacity and his future income due to the accidental injury which results in permanent disability.

Considering the medical reports,
discharge summary and oral testimony of PW1 to 3, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 85% and functional disability as 100%.
The monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.20,333/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 53 years as per the entry in Aadhar card which is at Ex P.20.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "11".

It is true that petitioner has lost his future income, accordingly he is entitled for future prospectus as per the dictum laid by the Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Sidaram Vs Divisional Manager,
United India Insurance Co.Ltd.

entities.text:
Sidaram Vs Divisional Manager,
United India Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And another reported in (2023)3 SCC 439 .
The said principle is also observed and applied by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No.100899/2024 order dated 19.06.2024.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for 15% future prospectus as he is 53 years of age and he is married.

Therefore the loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows; Rs.20,333/-(Monthly income) + 15% future prospectus (20,333+3050)=23383.00 monthly income is Rs.23,383/- X 12 (Months) X 11 (Multiplier) X 85% (Functional Disability) =
Rs.26,23,572/- Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.26,23,572/- as compensation under this head.
Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
18. It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury and it is grievous in nature.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries he has forgone certain amenities available for him.
There fore I award Rs.40,000/- under these conventional heads.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
19.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him before accident.
Therefore I award Rs.40,000/- as compensation under this head.
According to PW-3, petitioner is a need of artificial limb and its maintenance and petitioner has tendered estimation for the same as per Ex.P.19 and he has not examined author of the said document.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,00,000/- for artificial limb, its maintenance and future treatment.

ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
